title: The menu bar
text: Free space and a small storage bar, with what the last scan found. Scan Now starts a scan without opening the window. Clean Safe Items deletes every Safe suggestion Reclaim can delete, then shows a notification with the space freed. Open Reclaim , Settings and Quit. Hide it with Show Reclaim in the menu bar . Scheduled scans and alerts keep running while Reclaim is open, even with its window closed.

title: Scheduled scans
text: Choose Every day or Every week in Automation › Scan automatically . A scan runs when one is due, including right after your Mac wakes, and by default only sends a notification such as “12.4 GB can be reclaimed, 3.1 GB of it Safe.”

title: Auto-clean
text: Off by default, and the only time Reclaim deletes something nobody ticked at that moment. When Delete Safe items untouched for a day is on, each scheduled scan deletes: only Safe items, never Rebuild or Personal ones; only items you can delete without the helper; only items where nothing inside changed for 24 hours, so a project you are working in keeps its caches. It follows your Trash setting and is recorded in the history, and a notification tells you what was freed.

title: Low-space alerts
text: Reclaim checks free space every few minutes and notifies you once when it drops below your threshold, 10 GB by default, and again only after it has recovered and dropped again.

title: Open at login
text: Turn on Open at login in Automation so the menu bar and schedules are always running. If macOS asks you to approve it, Reclaim shows a button to Login Items in System Settings.

title: Notifications
text: The first time you turn on a schedule or low-space alerts, macOS asks whether Reclaim may send notifications. You can change this later in System Settings › Notifications .

title: What you need
text: The docker command and a running engine: OrbStack , Docker Desktop , Colima or another. Reclaim finds the command in the usual places, even when it is opened from Finder. Open Containers in the sidebar. If the engine is not running, start it and click Refresh .

title: What is listed
text: Item What it is Removed with Level Build cache Layers kept to speed up builds, not used by any image now. One item. docker builder prune --all Safe Dangling image An untagged image left behind when a newer build took its tag. docker image rm Safe Unused image A tagged image no container uses. Pulled or built again when needed. docker image rm Rebuild Stopped container A container that is not running. Changes made inside it are lost. docker container rm Rebuild Unused volume A volume no container uses. These often hold databases. docker volume rm Personal Images, containers and volumes that are in use are never listed. Select a row to read what it is and what happens after removing it.

title: How removal works
text: Ticked items are removed with Docker's own commands, never forced, so Docker itself refuses anything a container is using. Reclaim never touches the engine's disk image directly. Docker items share the Delete bar and the history with everything else. If Docker refuses an item, the summary shows Docker's reason and the item stays in the list.

title: About the sizes
text: Sizes come from docker system df . For an image, Reclaim shows the space only that image uses, which is what removing it frees; layers shared with other images stay. Totals can differ slightly from Docker's own summary because Docker rounds each size it reports.

title: Disk Map
text: The whole scan as folders and files, largest first. Each row has a bar for its share of the folder you are in, its size, the number of files inside and when anything in it last changed. Go deeper: double-click a folder, or right-click it and choose Open . Go back: click any folder in the trail at the top, or the up arrow in the toolbar ( ⌘ ↑ ). Tick anything that is not protected. Protected folders, such as the top level of the disk or your home folder, have a dimmed checkbox. Badges mark folders a rule already suggests. A lock means a folder could not be read, so its size is a lower bound. Small files under 1 MB are not listed one by one; their total appears below the list.

title: Large Files
text: Files of 500 MB or more that no other suggestion covers. Files inside apps and photo libraries are left out, because deleting part of a bundle breaks it. Everything here is Personal : only you know whether you still need it. Change the size in Scanning › Large files from ; the list updates at once.

title: Duplicates
text: After a scan, open Duplicates and click Find Duplicates . Reclaim compares files of 1 MB or more and lists only files whose contents are identical, byte for byte.

title: How duplicates are found
text: By size. Files with a unique size cannot have a twin, so they are dropped first. By their edges. The first and last 64 KB of the remaining files are compared. By full contents. Only the candidates left are read in full and compared by SHA-256. On a typical Mac this takes seconds.

title: What it leaves out
text: Anything inside apps, libraries and other bundles. Hidden folders such as ~/.vscode , and installed packages such as node_modules and site-packages : copies there belong to tools, and deleting one can break them. App and system data in ~/Library , /Library and /Users/Shared . Anything another suggestion already covers.

title: Hard links and APFS copies
text: Hard links are one file with several names, so they never appear as duplicates. APFS copies , such as those made with Finder's Duplicate, can share storage with the original. Reclaim detects them from where their data sits on disk and marks them Shares storage . Deleting one frees almost nothing, so they don't count towards the reclaimable total.

title: Choosing which copy to keep
text: Nothing is ticked for you. Each group shows every copy with its folder and date. The Keep menu in the toolbar ticks all but one copy in every group shown: Keep Oldest Copy or Keep Newest Copy , by modification date. Keep the Copy in a Folder… : choose a folder; in groups with a copy there, that copy is kept. Untick All Copies . Filter first to apply Keep to only some groups. Right-click a copy for Keep Only This Copy . If every copy in a group is ticked, the group shows a warning: deleting them all leaves you with none.

title: Safety
text: Why is there no "Are you sure?" Because cleaning a developer Mac means deleting hundreds of items, and a confirmation for each one gets clicked through without reading. Instead, Reclaim explains every item before you tick it, ticks only Safe items for you, and refuses to delete protected folders at all. If you want a safety net, turn on Move to Trash . Will Reclaim ever delete things on its own? Only if you turn on auto-clean for scheduled scans, which is off by default. Even then it deletes only Safe items that nothing changed for 24 hours. How auto-clean works . Can I undo a deletion? Not when deleting permanently, which is the default. With Move to Trash on, items go to the Trash and you can put them back from there until you empty it. Is it safe to delete Safe items while I am working? Usually. Quit an app before deleting its cache, and stop a dev server before deleting its project's build cache. Otherwise the app may recreate files mid-way or show errors until restarted. Why was something not deleted? The summary after deleting gives the reason for each item. Most often the files belong to root, for example ones created with sudo npm install . Install the helper to delete those. Files macOS itself protects cannot be deleted by any app. Is a helper that runs as root safe? It deletes only inside system cache and log folders and your own home folder, never a protected folder, and refuses tricks with .. and symlinks. It only answers the exact copy of Reclaim that installed it. The source is public, and you can remove it any time from System.

title: Protected folders
text: These are never deleted as a whole, however the path is written: with different capital letters, through a symlink, or as /System/Volumes/Data/… . Everything inside them, apart from the system folders, can still be deleted. The disk root, and every folder directly in it, such as /Applications , /Library , /Users and /opt . Everything in /System , /usr (except /usr/local ), /bin and /sbin . The folders directly in /private , and system folders such as /Library/Caches and /opt/homebrew . Every user's home folder, and every mounted volume in /Volumes . In your home: Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Movies, Music, Pictures, Public, Applications, the Trash, Library, and Library's main folders such as Application Support, Caches, Containers and Preferences. Separately, macOS itself stops any app from changing its system files.

title: Sizes
text: Why do Reclaim's sizes differ from Finder's? Reclaim shows the space files actually take on disk. Finder often shows how long files are. They differ for sparse files such as virtual machine disks, which can claim 64 GB while using a few, and for small files, which still occupy at least one disk block. Hard-linked files are counted once. Why doesn't free space go up by exactly what I deleted? Some reasons: files that were APFS copies of each other shared their storage; local Time Machine snapshots still hold the deleted data until macOS removes them; and macOS counts "purgeable" space as free. The figure settles within a few minutes. Why doesn't the scan total match the used space? Folders Reclaim cannot read are missing from the total (give it Full Disk Access ), and the disk also holds snapshots and file-system data that are not files.

title: Permissions
text: Why does it need Full Disk Access? macOS hides other apps' data, Mail, Messages and parts of your Library from apps by default. Without access, those folders are not measured or suggested. Reclaim works without it, but sees less. Why are my Desktop, Documents and Downloads missing from the scan? Reclaim does not have Full Disk Access yet. Without it, macOS shows a permission dialog for each of those folders and holds the scan until you answer, so Reclaim skips them instead. Turn on Full Disk Access and scan again. Why isn't it in the Mac App Store? App Store apps run in a sandbox that cannot read or delete files across the disk, which is the whole point of Reclaim. Why does macOS block it the first time? The app is not notarized, which requires a paid Apple developer membership. Follow Open it the first time , or build it from source.

title: Privacy
text: Does Reclaim send anything over the network? No. It has no account, no analytics and no update check. The scan and your file list stay on your Mac. Its only files are its settings and the deletion history .

title: Scanning
text: Click Scan on the Overview, or press ⌘ R . Reclaim reads every folder it is allowed to and shows a live count of files and bytes. A full Mac takes about a minute; click Stop at any time. Whole disk by default. To scan only your home folder, change Scanning › Scan . Real sizes. Reclaim counts the space files actually use. A 32 GB disk image holding 1 GB counts as 1 GB, and a file with several hard links counts once. One disk only. External drives and other volumes are never scanned. Without Full Disk Access , Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive and other apps' data are skipped so macOS doesn't pause the scan to ask about each. Turn it on .

title: The Overview
text: Storage bar: used space, the part Reclaim suggests deleting in your accent colour, and free space. Last scan: how much you could reclaim, how much of it is Safe, and how long the scan took. Top categories: each kind of suggestion with its size. Click one to open it.

title: Reviewing suggestions
text: The sidebar has one entry per kind of suggestion with its total size. What it finds lists every rule. Each list shows a checkbox, the item's name and folder, its size, its safety level and when anything inside it last changed. Sort by clicking a column header, and filter with the search field ( ⌘ F ). Select All Safe ticks every Safe item in the list; Deselect All unticks the list. Right-click rows to tick or untick several at once, or to reveal one in Finder. The inspector on the right explains the selected item: what it is, why it is suggested, what happens after deleting it, and where it is. Show or hide it with the toolbar button. An orange warning next to an app's cache means that app is running. Quit it before deleting its files. A lock means the item belongs to root; deleting it needs the helper .

title: Safety levels
text: Level Meaning Ticked for you Safe Rebuilds itself; nothing for you to do. Build caches, app caches, logs, emulator quick-boot snapshots, the Trash. Yes Rebuild Comes back after a reinstall or download, such as npm install or composer install . No Personal Your data, reported so you can decide: old downloads, large files, duplicates, emulator user data, leftovers of uninstalled apps. No To stop Reclaim ticking Safe items after each scan, turn off Tick Safe items after each scan .

title: Deleting
text: Whenever something is ticked, a bar at the bottom shows how many items and how much space, such as Delete 23 items · 31.4 GB . Ticks carry across every list, the Disk Map, Duplicates and Containers, and an item inside a ticked folder is never counted twice. There is no confirmation. The button, or ⌘ ⌫ , deletes ticked items immediately and permanently. For a safety net, turn on Move to Trash instead of deleting permanently . Space is then freed only when you empty the Trash. A sheet shows progress, then a summary of what was freed and anything that could not be removed, with the reason: Belongs to another user , such as root: files created with sudo or by the system. The helper can delete these. It no longer exists: something else removed it after the scan. Protected: one of the folders Reclaim never deletes as a whole. See the FAQ . Lists and the Disk Map update straight away; no rescan is needed.

title: History
text: Every run is recorded: when, what was deleted or moved to the Trash, its size and anything that failed. The log is kept at ~/Library/Application Support/Reclaim/history.jsonl .

title: Keyboard shortcuts
text: Shortcut Action ⌘ R Scan ⌘ ⌫ Delete ticked items, with no confirmation ⌘ F Filter the current list ⌘ ↑ Enclosing folder in the Disk Map ⌘ , Settings

title: Reclaim home
text: v0.1.0 Free and open source for macOS 14+ Your Mac is full of things you don't need. Reclaim scans the whole disk, explains what is safe to delete, and frees the space in one click. Built for developer Macs that fill up with build caches, node_modules , simulators and Docker leftovers. Download for Mac Read the docs MIT licensed Apple silicon and Intel No account or tracking Reclaim 0.0 GB reclaim

title: Install
text: Download the latest release Reclaim.zip from GitHub Releases Build it yourself From source with Xcode

title: Requirements
text: macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Apple silicon or Intel. The app is a universal binary. It is tested on Apple silicon.

title: Download
text: Get the app. Open the latest release and download Reclaim.zip , plus Reclaim.zip.sha256 if you want to check it. Optional: check the download. In Terminal, in the folder you downloaded to, run the command below. It should print Reclaim.zip: OK . shasum -a 256 -c Reclaim.zip.sha256 Move it to Applications. Double-click Reclaim.zip and drag Reclaim into your Applications folder.

title: Open it the first time
text: Reclaim is not notarized by Apple, because notarization needs a paid developer membership, so macOS blocks it the first time. You do this once per version. Try to open it. Double-click Reclaim in Applications. macOS says it cannot verify the app. Click Done . Open Privacy & Security. Go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and scroll to the Security section. Allow it. Next to the message about Reclaim, click Open Anyway and confirm with your password or Touch ID. The source is public, so you can also build it yourself instead of trusting a download.

title: Give it Full Disk Access
text: Without it, macOS asks for permission the first time any app opens Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive or another app's data, and the app has to wait for your answer. To keep scans from stalling, Reclaim skips those folders until it has Full Disk Access, and the Overview says so with a button to the right settings page. Open the setting. Go to System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access . Add Reclaim. Click + , choose Reclaim in Applications, and make sure its switch is on. Scan again. Quit and reopen Reclaim, then scan. No app can grant this to itself, and Reclaim never asks again once it is on. Your Music, TV and Photos libraries are always skipped, even with Full Disk Access, because macOS protects them with permissions of their own. Reclaim never suggests anything inside them.

title: Updating
text: Download the new release and replace the old app in Applications. Because each build is signed separately, macOS may ask you to repeat Open Anyway , you may need to switch Full Disk Access off and on again, and the helper , if you use it, asks to be paired again.

title: Uninstalling
text: Remove the helper , if you installed it: open System in the sidebar and click Remove Helper… . Remove the app. Quit Reclaim and move it from Applications to the Trash. Optional: remove its settings and history. rm ~/Library/Preferences/io.github.kstmostofa.reclaim.plist rm -r ~/Library/Application\ Support/Reclaim Tidy up permissions. Remove it from Full Disk Access and, if you turned it on, from Login Items in System Settings.

title: Building from source
text: You need Xcode and XcodeGen . brew install xcodegen git clone https://github.com/kstmostofa/reclaim.git cd reclaim xcodegen generate open Reclaim.xcodeproj The engine's tests run with swift test in Packages/ReclaimCore . They only ever create and delete files in temporary folders.

title: General
text: Setting What it does Default Move to Trash instead of deleting permanently Ticked items go to the Trash, so you can put them back. Space is freed only when you empty it. Items that need the helper are left alone in this mode. Off Tick Safe items after each scan Safe items are ticked as soon as a scan finishes. Rebuild and Personal items never are. On Restore Default Settings Resets every setting on every tab. —

title: Scanning
text: Setting What it does Default Scan The whole disk, or only your home folder. The whole disk also finds system caches and leftovers outside your home. Whole disk Large files from The size from which a file appears in Large Files. The list updates as you change it. 500 MB Old downloads after How long a file in Downloads must be unchanged before it is suggested. 90 days Compare duplicates from The smallest file Duplicates compares. 1 MB Never scan these folders Folders skipped completely: nothing in them is measured, suggested or deletable. None Scope, the downloads age and excluded folders take effect at the next scan.

title: Automation
text: Setting What it does Default Show Reclaim in the menu bar Free space, the last scan, Scan Now and Clean Safe Items in the menu bar. On Open at login Starts Reclaim when you log in, so the menu bar and schedules are always on. Off Scan automatically Never, every day or every week, while Reclaim is open. Never Delete Safe items untouched for a day After each scheduled scan, deletes Safe items that nothing changed for 24 hours. Details . Off Warn when free space is low A notification once each time free space drops below the threshold. On Warn below The free-space threshold for that warning. 10 GB

title: Appearance
text: Setting What it does Default Appearance Follow the system, or always light or dark. System Accent color The colour of buttons, selections and the reclaimable part of the storage bar. Twelve presets. Indigo Custom color Pick any colour; Reclaim switches to it. —

title: What the helper handles
text: System caches in /Library/Caches . System logs in /Library/Logs and /private/var/log . Root-owned files in your home folder , such as those left by sudo npm install . Local Time Machine snapshots . Items that need the helper show a lock until it is installed, and Safe ones are only ticked for you once it is.

title: Installing
text: Open System. Click System in the sidebar, then Install Helper… . Enter your password. macOS asks in its own dialog. Reclaim never sees it. The helper is copied to /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools and started by macOS whenever Reclaim needs it. After that, deleting works as usual: anything Reclaim may not delete is passed to the helper automatically when deleting permanently. In Move to Trash mode, such items are left alone.

title: What keeps it safe
text: Fixed folders only System cache and log folders and your own home folder, after resolving symlinks. Never a protected folder. No path tricks Paths with .. are refused, and so is a folder swapped for a link at the last moment. One app only Paired with the exact build of Reclaim that installed it. Any other program is refused. Open source The helper is small, and its rules are tested. Read it on GitHub.

title: After updating Reclaim
text: The pairing names one exact build, so after an update the helper refuses the new version. System then shows Pair Again… , which asks for your password once more. A paid Apple developer certificate would remove this step.

title: Local Time Machine snapshots
text: Time Machine keeps snapshots on your Mac's disk between backups, and they hold on to the space of files you deleted since. System lists them; with the helper installed you can tick and delete them. Backups on your backup disk are not affected, and macOS also removes local snapshots on its own when space runs low.

title: Removing the helper
text: Click Remove Helper… in System and enter your password. Everything else in Reclaim keeps working without it.

title: What it finds
text: ~ means your home folder.

title: Build Caches
text: Output your project's tooling recreates on the next build or dev-server start. That first build is slower. What Matched when Level Next.js build cache .next beside a package.json Safe Nuxt build cache .nuxt beside a package.json Safe SvelteKit build cache .svelte-kit beside a package.json Safe Turborepo cache any .turbo folder Safe Parcel cache any .parcel-cache folder Safe Dart tool cache .dart_tool beside a pubspec.yaml Safe Python bytecode cache any __pycache__ folder Safe Rust build output target beside a Cargo.toml Safe Gradle project cache .gradle beside a build.gradle , build.gradle.kts or settings file Safe Android build intermediates build/intermediates ; built APKs and bundles in build/outputs are kept Safe Xcode DerivedData each project folder in ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData Safe

title: Dependencies
text: Packages your project installed. Run the install command again before using the project. What Matched when To get it back Level Node packages node_modules beside a package.json npm install , pnpm install or yarn Rebuild Composer packages vendor beside a composer.json composer install Rebuild CocoaPods Pods beside a Podfile pod install Rebuild Python virtual environment venv , .venv or env containing pyvenv.cfg python -m venv and reinstall requirements Rebuild Packages that tools installed for themselves are skipped: anything in a hidden folder in your home (such as ~/.vscode/extensions or ~/.composer ), in ~/Library , or in system and Homebrew locations. Deleting those would break the tool, and there is no project to reinstall into.

title: Package Caches
text: Downloads shared by every project, kept so they need not be fetched again. Deleting them only costs a re-download the next time a project needs them. What Location Level npm cache ~/.npm/_cacache Safe pnpm store ~/Library/pnpm/store Safe Yarn cache ~/Library/Caches/Yarn Safe pip cache ~/Library/Caches/pip Safe Composer cache ~/Library/Caches/composer , ~/.composer/cache Safe Gradle caches and wrapper downloads ~/.gradle/caches , ~/.gradle/wrapper/dists Safe Homebrew downloads ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew Safe CocoaPods cache ~/Library/Caches/CocoaPods Safe Cargo downloads and sources ~/.cargo/registry/cache , ~/.cargo/registry/src Safe Go build cache ~/Library/Caches/go-build Safe Dart and Flutter packages ~/.pub-cache ; run flutter pub get afterwards, and re-activate global tools Rebuild Playwright browsers ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright ; run npx playwright install afterwards Rebuild

title: App Caches and Logs
text: What Location Level App cache each folder in ~/Library/Caches . The app rebuilds it and may start slower once. Safe Logs each item in ~/Library/Logs , including crash reports Safe If the app a cache belongs to is running, the item shows a warning. Quit the app first.

title: Mobile Tooling
text: What Matched when After deleting Level Android emulator snapshots snapshots inside an emulator folder (beside its config.ini ) The emulator cold-boots once Safe Android emulator user data userdata-qemu.img in an emulator folder The emulator starts as if factory reset Personal iOS device support each version in ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/iOS DeviceSupport Xcode copies it again when that device is connected Rebuild Simulator caches ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches Recreated when needed Safe

title: App Leftovers
text: Folders in ~/Library/Containers and ~/Library/Application Support named after an app's identifier (such as com.docker.docker ) when no installed app has that identifier. Apple's own folders are never included, and an extension's folder counts as its app's. Personal If you reinstall the app later, it starts without its old settings and data.

title: Trash and Old Downloads
text: What Matched when Level In the Trash each item in your Trash. Deleting it is the same as emptying the Trash. Safe Old download each item in ~/Downloads not changed for 90 days (adjustable) Personal

title: Large Files
text: Files of 500 MB or more (adjustable) that no rule above covers, outside apps and photo libraries. Personal

title: Docker
text: From Docker's own disk-usage report, when an engine is running. See Containers . What Removed with Level Build cache not used by any image docker builder prune --all Safe Dangling images docker image rm Safe Unused images docker image rm Rebuild Stopped containers docker container rm Rebuild Unused volumes docker volume rm Personal

title: System Junk
text: Most of these belong to root, so deleting them needs the helper . Items macOS protects are skipped even then. What Location Level System cache each folder in /Library/Caches Safe System logs each item in /Library/Logs and /private/var/log Safe Safe items that need the helper are only ticked for you once it is installed.

title: Never suggested or deleted
text: Anything inside an app, framework, photo or music library, or other bundle is never suggested on its own. Folders you list under Never scan these folders . Your Music, TV and Photos libraries, which macOS protects with permissions of their own. Protected folders, which cannot be deleted as a whole from anywhere in the app. See the FAQ for the list.
